name: Epsio
tagline: An incremental view engine that keeps complex SQL results fresh inside your existing Postgres or MySQL.
description: Epsio sits beside an existing database, reads its replication stream, and maintains the results of expensive SQL queries incrementally, writing them back into a regular results table in the same database. Applications just query that table, so there is no new query endpoint to adopt. It targets Postgres, MySQL and SQL Server users who use materialized views or denormalized caches that are slow to refresh. It runs inside your cloud account and data does not leave your environment. It is a small, commercial startup product with little public release information, so evaluate it carefully before you depend on it.

pricing.notes: Free start option; pricing not published.

strengths: Results land in normal tables in your existing database
No new query engine for applications to adopt
Handles joins and aggregations incrementally from CDC
weaknesses: Little public release information and a small vendor
Results lag the source by replication delay
Adds write load to the primary when writing results back
useCases: Speeding up slow dashboards and reports on OLTP Postgres
Replacing REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW cron jobs
notIdealFor: Streaming from Kafka or non-database sources
